explain.say: Tides are not the same size every day. Over about two weeks they swing from extra big to quite small and back, because the Sun's gravity adds to or works against the Moon's.

explain.say: At new moon and full moon, the Sun, Earth and Moon line up. Their pulls add together, making spring tides, with the highest high tides and the lowest low tides. They have nothing to do with the season spring.

explain.say: About a week later, at half moon, the Sun and Moon pull at right angles to each other. Their effects partly cancel, giving neap tides, with the smallest difference between high and low water.

explain.say: So there are two spring tides and two neap tides every lunar month of about 29 and a half days. Sailors, fishers and coastal engineers plan around this rhythm.

faq.q: Why are they called spring tides?
faq.a: The name comes from the water seeming to spring up, not from the season. Spring tides happen twice every month, all year round.
asks: Do spring tides happen in spring?

faq.a: At new moon and full moon, when the Sun, Earth and Moon are lined up and their pulls on the oceans add together.
A neap tide happens at half moon, when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles. Their pulls partly cancel, so high tides are lower and low tides are higher than usual.
Tidal range is the height difference between high tide and low tide. It is biggest at spring tides and smallest at neap tides.
asks: How much does the tide go up and down?

faq.a: King tide is a popular name for the very highest spring tides of the year, when the Moon is also near its closest to Earth. They can flood low-lying coastal streets.
asks: What is a perigean spring tide?

facts: Spring tides come about every 14 to 15 days, at new moon and full moon.
The lunar month, from one full moon to the next, lasts about 29.5 days.

quiz.say: The Moon is full tonight. What kind of tide is expected?
quiz.why: At full moon the Sun, Earth and Moon are lined up, so their pulls add together into a spring tide.

wrong.1: Neap tides come at half moon, when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles.
wrong.2: There are tides every day; the Moon's phase only changes how big they are.
